paths._notes: project_root is resolved per-instance via config, not hardcoded (the real instance root is data/*/career/ per the framework's generic-glob convention). applications_csv lives directly at project_root, not under applications/ -- it's the living/primary tracker, not historical data; its actual filename is instance-specific. Everything else under paths is historical/pipeline data and lives inside applications/.

gmail.query: (from:jobalert@linkedin.com OR from:alerts@indeed.com OR from:alerts@ziprecruiter.com OR from:no-reply@flexjobs.com OR from:noreply@jobs.lever.co OR from:greenhouse.io OR subject:"job alert" OR subject:"new jobs for you" OR subject:"jobs matching" OR subject:"recommended jobs")
gmail._notes: lookback_days: 1 = today's emails only (steady-state daily cron). 3 = catch-up window on first run or after a skipped day. known_senders are senders whose tracked redirect URLs are known to land on usable ATS pages; other senders get their canonical URL resolved by following the redirect. Tune query if you add or remove alert sources.

scraper._notes: playwright_hosts are ATS hosts the local Playwright scraper can handle. Greenhouse is SSR (web_fetch already works there too; Playwright is a harmless fallback). Lever is client-rendered and empty via web_fetch, so Playwright is the only local option. Workday and Ashby are listed but should be confirmed per-tenant before relying on them. ZipRecruiter, Indeed, and FlexJobs need the persistent browser_profile/ login session to get past bot walls reliably. skip_hosts (LinkedIn) is excluded because the interactive session's Chrome-extension same-origin fetch recipe (see README.md) returns cleaner structured text than any local scrape.

pipeline._notes: Daily caps: triage roughly 10-12 jobs per run, letters roughly 2-3 per run. Letters dominate compute cost, so the two caps are tracked separately. Set playwright_headless to false only for debugging or the one-time login flow.
